items.reported: السماء has an extra fatha and lost the kasra sitting directly under its hamza; the kasra leaked to the next word and was named fatha
items.cause: a mutual exchange across a word boundary. Both halves had to move together, but the reverse half was never proposed: the guard skipped any mark whose `line` TAG differed from its word's, and this kasra hangs low enough to be tagged to the next line while being drawn inside its own line's band.

items.reported: did we audit our ligature tags and find where we have issues?
items.cause: n/a
items.detail: Built: `tools/audit_ligatures.py`, over 159,327 groups in 77,429 words. count 2,455 (a word emits a different number of groups than the joining rules allow) | empty 732 (names letters, holds no ink) | misplaced 1,220 (a mark on another group's letters) | order 79. Of the 732 empty, 521 name a lone `ا`, which this art may legitimately draw inside the preceding ligature — those are the joining model disagreeing with the drawing, not lost ink. 56 name a multi-letter piece and 18 name a `ء`: those are real. A detector only; no corrector yet.

items.reported: the kasra is under the tag data-text="وا" not "لسما", and that group now holds لسماء not لسما — either move the kasra and rename, or give the hamza its own group with its kasra. How many similar cases are in the data?
items.cause: two separate faults. The first is mine: the four passes I added this session appended a moved mark to `at[0]`, the word's FIRST ligature group, instead of the group whose ink it sits over — `_omove`, which every older mover uses, picks the nearest atom. The second predates them: `segment_word` cuts وَٱلسَّمَآءِ into ['و','ا','لسما','ء'] and the hamza's ink is emitted inside the `لسما` group, leaving `ء` empty.
items.detail: Routing fixed — all four passes now call `put_in_ligature()`, the same nearest-atom rule, so the kasra lands with the hamza. The empty `ء` group is a real defect and 18 words share it; the audit that finds them is now `tools/audit_ligatures.py`. Correcting it is not written.

items.reported: our quran svg version draws iqlab as SINGLE diacritic + meem, not double diacritic (tanween pair) + meem — audit every place that assumes otherwise
items.cause: confirmed. uthmani writes tanween+meem (U+064C U+06E2), the KFGQPC text of this print writes single haraka+meem (U+064F U+06E2), the ink draws the single stroke. assign_words.py:4917 knows this but exits early ('already named') before rescuing the meem when the shape table has already named the tanween — the meem stays counted as a letter piece: the 12 CERTAIN ligature-surplus words. Full site survey in docs/defects/iqlab_notation.md
items.status: FIXED 2026-08-26: _IQTAN no longer exits early; the next-word meem claim may claim a word's own piece; a late position-aware self-rescue (QSVG_IQLATE) runs before QSVG_IQFIX, anchored on the word's own tanween. 10 of 12 surplus words fixed (p203/p219 were pen-lift false positives, see item 19). Bench cases added for p143/p222. Side effect: +32 interval flags = naming visibility on tight-kerned iqlab pairs, mark budgets clean; p437 بِيضٌۭ holds a second م-shaped piece at its word START — needs a visual verdict.

items.reported: these ligature-surplus CERTAIN flags are actually correct words — one ligature is thin at the middle, so maybe counted as 2?
items.cause: confirmed by measurement: the stroke thins to a pen-lift and the one calligraphic stroke is two contours. Their boxes OVERLAP end-to-end (x-overlap 1.4-4.7u with y-overlap), while genuinely foreign pieces have POSITIVE gaps (p451 إِلْ يَاسِينَ: +1.0..+3.3u) — an empty band. Effective-piece counting in audit_marks.py and score_confidence.py now clusters bodies whose boxes overlap (x>0.5u, y>3u) before counting. p589 يَسْجُدُونَ cleared by the same rule; p451 still flags, correctly.

items.reported: we don't compare with the correct text of the mushaf: the print has two words بعد and ما with ما on the following line, but we link them as a single word بعد ما
items.cause: confirmed. quran.com's layout carries بَعْدَ مَا as ONE word on line 6; the print draws بعد at line 6's end and ما at line 7's start. The pipeline cannot split a word across a line boundary, so it forced the whole word onto line 7 — بعد's ink on line 6 was folded into أَهْوَآءَهُم (4/5 pieces, the audit counting بعد's marks in its budget) and the word took a piece from جَآءَكَ (2/3). One mis-expressible word shears BOTH lines: the 12-word 0.47x width cluster, the mushaf's only rtl-order flag, and the interval flags on this page are all this. The letter-space compound family has 5 members; only this one straddles a line break.
items.status: diagnosed, fix in plan (allow a letter-space compound to split at the space across the line boundary during reflow/clustering; check how MushafDatabase segments it before choosing the emission shape)
